rows.title: Bang
notes: 2026 Steel City Dance Discs

rows.title: Mudanin Kata
notes: “this one by david darling and wulu uh bunyan or bunan bunan ... this track uh very specially titled ... mudanin kata”
2004 Riverboat Records album pairing cellist David Darling with the Wulu Bunun people of Taiwan; 'Mudanin Kata' is the real release/track title.
“towards the end of the show for any indigenous listeners there is a song by a bark and g man who passed away in 2023”

rows.title: Belly Is Psychic
notes: “second we had belly is psychic by punker great statue and half strange which they recorded at orotanga station it's a really beautiful compilation you can find on spotify”
Punko is a real Australian artist tied to the 2023 'Half Strange' outback-station recording tour/compilation, though the exact track title couldn't be independently verified.

rows.title: Clouds and Pulses
notes: “this last song was by stefan sobel he is a composer an improviser guitar player and an avant-garde musician ... it's from a release uh 21st of june called clouds and pulses”
the audio briefly looked like Aureum - Distance, but the presenter said otherwise
2023 organ album 'Clouds and Pulses' by Slovak composer Štefan Szabó on Czech label MA Records.

rows.title: Nád Jancsi (Jancsi of the Reeds)
notes: “it's by Visenta Group. The song is called Nod Yonchi, Yonchi of the Reeds. It's a band that started in Budapest in 1967. ... Let's take a listen to it now.”
Track on Vízöntő's 1987 Hungaroton album 'Villanypásztor'; band actually formed in Budapest in 1976, not 1967 as stated on air.
“And up at the top, that was... Visunter Group. The Budapest band from 1967, kind of tying in experimental music and classical Hungarian folk music.”
Same Hungarian avant-folk band as entry 5; no distinct track title given on air for this mention.

rows.title: Black Horse
notes: “So before that we had Gastra del Sol, Black Horse. It's a project by Jim O'Rourke, who you spoke to.”
Track on Gastr del Sol's 1998 album 'Camoufleur', the duo of David Grubbs and Jim O'Rourke.

rows.title: Zorba's Dance
notes: 1965 Sony Music Entertainment Greece

rows.title: Hooray For Another Day
notes: “and so this is max oaks ... hooray for another day an excellent album especially if you like um kind of classical folk uh american or total island and finger-picking style”
Tompkins Square album by American Primitive fingerstyle guitarist Max Ochs.

rows.title: Dream Songs
notes: “this is a project by Robert Sotelo and Mary Currie ... this project that they came out with called Dream Songs. It was released in 2024, in October”
4-track 7" EP on Upset The Rhythm, released 25 Oct 2024.

rows.title: I Want You To Know Me
notes: 2021 Stroom

rows.title: This Thread Is A Green Street
notes: 2024 Bella Union

rows.title: Nu Stone Groove
notes: 2025 Efficient Space

rows.title: Al Daw' (Nothing Comes Back the Same)
notes: “So that was an artist called Maya Al-Khadi. Yes, Aldor, or it's also titled Nothing Comes Back the Same, from an album called Otherworld”
Opening track of Maya Al Khaldi's 2022 album 'Other World' (Tawleef); 'Aldor' is ASR mangling of 'Al Daw''.

rows.title: Yaykatekar Dub (Love Dub)
notes: 2004 Mais Um Discos

rows.title: King and Country
notes: “before that we had the space padlocks king and country”
Real punk trio from Toulouse, France with several EPs/demos on Bandcamp; exact track title taken on trust from the announcement.
“So sick. Radio Dello.”

rows.title: Agadez
notes: “this one's called agadez by etran deler”
Tuareg/Saharan rock band from Agadez, Niger; 'Agadez' is the title of their 2022 album on Sahel Sounds/Fat Cat.

rows.title: Desire
notes: “Before that, we had Mope Grooves, really, yeah, just a classic album for me. The song's called Desire.”
Portland guitar-rock band's 2019 album 'Desire' includes a title track matching the description.

rows.title: Indoctrination
notes: “Household name. Indoctrination is the song name from a compilation called The Art School Dance Goes On, Leeds post-punk 1977 to 84”
Appears on Caroline True Records compilation 'The Art School Dance Goes On: Leeds Post-Punk 1977-84', exactly as described.

rows.title: Baakintji Dreaming
notes: “This is Songbird's Four Ballads Behind Bars. It's called Bakanji Dreaming by a man called Anzac. ... here it comes.”
Track by Anzac, a Baakintji man who died in custody in 2023, on the Songbirds 'Ballads Behind Bars' prison-songwriting project (CRC NSW).

rows.title: Not a Second Time
notes: 1980 Island Records

rows.title: Hold On
notes: 1999 Anti/Epitaph

rows.title: Slovenia Inshallah (track: Serhat's Testimony)
notes: “And then before that was Slovenia, Inshallah, by Masa Nazal and Iye Shtita. Serhat's testimony, again, off Glark.”
mentioned by the presenter but we couldn't work out when it played
Mixtape on the GLARC label documenting EU border-violence testimonies, includes a track literally titled 'Serhat's testimony'.
